ops.title: apply: request params lose odd microseconds of ChromeMicros expiries ≥ 2^53 (synckit map[string]any decode)
ops.description: Found by the import design lane (2026-09-30, `recovery-20260930/cookiesync-linux/import-design.md` §4 and Pitfalls). synckit v0.37.0 decodes every request into `map[string]any` with plain `json.Unmarshal` (`synckit/rpc/protocol.go:51-57`, called from `rpc/server.go:42`), so JSON numbers become float64 and any ChromeMicros ≥ 2^53 (every real expiry) loses its odd microsecond. `cookiesync rpc apply` sends wire cookies as numbers (`internal/cli/rpc.go:160-183` → `wireCookiesParam`, `internal/daemon/handlers.go:761-780`), so an odd-microsecond expiry is written back off by one microsecond. Responses are unaffected (`Response.Result` stays `json.RawMessage`). The import primitive sidesteps this by sending its document as a JSON string; `apply` (a write path, out of the Linux port's scope) is not fixed there. Fix options: carry wire cookies as a string in `apply` params and decode with `readWireCookies` daemon-side, or use `json.Number`/RawMessage decoding in synckit. Also related: `unixSecondsToChromeMicros` (`internal/cookie/models.go:43-45`) is not an exact inverse of `chromeMicrosToUnix` (~2.4% of sampled expiries re-render differently); the import lane adds an exact `chromeMicrosFromUnix` without touching existing callers.

ops.text: `rpc apply` round-trips a cookie with an odd-microsecond expiry ≥ 2^53 byte-exactly (test with 15746918400015625)
No Darwin-visible behavior change beyond the fixed precision
